question: Can I reach you at 2am?
html:
We can't confirm that a person will answer at 2am. Our available information does not list overnight phone hours, so we won't promise live coverage we can't verify.

What we can confirm

  • Our records don't state when our phone lines are staffed overnight.
  • Our planning assumes some late-night calls go unanswered today. About 12% of calls are assumed to come after hours, and about 35% of those are assumed lost (est.) (Voice AI research).
  • Across our model, about 14.8% of all inbound calls are missed (est.), within a range of 10% to 35% (Voice AI research).

Why late calls matter

Urgent problems don't keep business hours. Late calls also rise when demand peaks.

SignalFigureSource
Off-hours share of HVAC inbound calls, June14.1%ServiceTitan, via Punctual Pros demand model
Off-hours share, October9.8%ServiceTitan, via Punctual Pros demand model
Peak off-hours window5–9 pm localPunctual Pros demand model
Off-hours calls trades typically lose30–40%Voice AI research
Home-services callers who reach a person52%Invoca 2026 benchmark, via Voice AI research

These are industry and modelled figures. They are not our measured 2am answer rate.

What would answer this

  • Our phone-system or ServiceTitan call logs, broken out by hour. These would show how many calls arrive between midnight and 6am and how many reach a person.
  • Booked jobs from those overnight calls. This would show whether overnight answering converts to work.
  • Our current after-hours staffing or answering-service schedule. This would give a direct yes or no.

The research also notes that AI voice agents can answer and book calls at any hour. Vendors report booking rates of 70% overall and 90% when capacity is open, against a typical human rate of 42% (Voice AI research). These vendor figures are self-reported and unaudited. We have not confirmed that we use such a system.

Every unanswered night call is a buyer who rings the next number on Google, and the model puts after-hours recovery alone at about $390,000 a year (est.) (Voice AI research).

Next actions

  1. Pull 12 months of call logs by hour and day. Measure the real overnight answer and booking rates against the 35% loss assumption.
  2. Confirm and publish our actual overnight answering policy, so this assistant can give a direct answer.
  3. Scope a pilot of an AI voice agent for overnight and storm overflow calls. Track booked jobs, not vendor-reported rates.
  4. Recheck the model's after-hours inputs once our own data is loaded, in line with the calibration step in the Punctual Pros demand model (Sep 24, 2026).
